intended_object: The conjugation map c_x : K → G, k ↦ x k x⁻¹, for an open subgroup K of a topological group G and an element x, as a continuous group homomorphism. In the Mackey decomposition it is used to form K ∩ x⁻¹Hx. Inferred from the name, the docstring and its use in Mackey.lean.
explanation: The body composes `(MulAut.conj x).toMonoidHom`, which sends g to x * g * x⁻¹, with the inclusion `K.subtype`. This gives exactly k ↦ x k x⁻¹ as a monoid homomorphism. Continuity comes from `IsTopologicalGroup.continuous_conj x` composed with `continuous_subtype_val`. The library takes `H.comap (mackeyConjugationHom K x)`, which is {k ∈ K : x k x⁻¹ ∈ H} = K ∩ x⁻¹Hx, the group the Mackey formula needs. Any subgroup K would work in place of an open one; restricting to `OpenSubgroup` just matches the setting of the surrounding file, so this is not a real narrowing. Mathlib has the underlying pieces (`MulAut.conj`, `IsTopologicalGroup.continuous_conj`); I did not search it for a ready-made continuous conjugation homomorphism from a subgroup, so no counterpart is cited.
